what: M6 Part A: offline RL with known truth (single-drive MDP)

hypotheses.H1_fqi_overestimates_rare_go: Naive tabular fitted Q iteration overestimates Q(go) where go is rarely or never logged: with coach-like data at the real size, its mean Q_hat(go) - Q*(go) is positive in the 0 and 1-9 count buckets and close to zero at 100+. Gradient-boosted FQI also overestimates there, by extrapolation. Tabular CQL's error in those buckets is negative.
hypotheses.H2_optimizers_curse: FQI and the plug-in overclaim the value of the actions they choose (claimed minus true value of the chosen action is positive), more for choices that differ from the coaches' usual action than for the usual ones, and the slope of the true gain on the claimed gain over the coaches' usual action is below 1.
hypotheses.H3_cql_beats_naive_fqi_on_coach_data: With coach-like data at the real size, CQL (main alpha) has lower true regret than naive tabular FQI.
hypotheses.H4_cql_inherits_conservatism: CQL is not automatically better. Under the very conservative behavior policy its true regret is higher than the plug-in's at the real size and above, because it stays close to the logged actions. Under uniform behavior every Q-based method's regret falls toward zero as data grows.
hypotheses.H5_deferring_to_coaches: Candidate headline 1 of the research note, in this known-truth world: at the real data size with coach-like behavior, deferring to coaches when unsure (behavior cloning's most common action, or the abstain rule at 83% bootstrap agreement) has higher true regret than the plug-in, so deferring loses more than it saves.
hypotheses.H6_bc_recovers_behavior: Behavior cloning's stochastic policy has nearly the behavior policy's regret once data is plentiful (within 0.01 points per drive at 1M decisions).
hypotheses.H7_d3rlpy: The d3rlpy network versions reproduce the tabular pattern: offline DoubleDQN overestimates rarely logged go actions and DiscreteCQL pushes them below Q*.
